question: Should OpenClaw core support cross-gateway session messaging directly, or should this remain a plugin/bridge capability until a broader federation contract is approved?
rationale: The requested behavior is missing, but the implementation shape affects gateway trust boundaries, session ownership, message delivery, and core-vs-plugin responsibility.

options.title: Design core contract first
options.body: Define the gateway-to-gateway identity, authorization, replay, and session-visibility contract before landing a core implementation.

options.title: Plugin or MCP bridge first
options.body: Keep core gateway-local and expose only missing plugin/API seams needed for external bridges to implement cross-gateway routing safely.

options.title: Wait for the broader FRD
options.body: Hold this concrete feature behind https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733 until maintainers settle transport and tenant-scoped operator policy.

recommendation.title: Design core contract first
recommendation.body: Define the gateway-to-gateway identity, authorization, replay, and session-visibility contract before landing a core implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail for session-tool architecture, gatewayUrl security, and session resolution points to this owner candidate.
